outlooks.summary: SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP FROM THE MIDDLE MISSOURI VALLEY REGION SOUTHWARD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS SUNDAY AFTERNOON...AND THEN WILL SPREAD EASTWARD ACROSS NEBRASKA/KANSAS AND VICINITY OVERNIGHT. THE MAIN THREATS WILL BE VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING STRAIGHT-LINE WINDS.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: UPPER RIDGING IS FORECAST TO PREVAIL E OF THE MS VALLEY SUNDAY...WHILE A MORE ACTIVE PATTERN IS EXPECTED UPSTREAM ACROSS THE PLAINS AND VICINITY. HERE...SHORT-WAVE TROUGHING IS FORECAST TO BEGIN SHIFTING INTO THE PLAINS IN SOMEWHAT PIECEMEAL FASHION -- INITIALLY INTO THE DAKOTAS/NEBRASKA EARLY IN THE PERIOD AND THEN LATER INTO THE CENTRAL PLAINS THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AND INTO THE EVENING. AT THE SURFACE...A COLD FRONT IS FORECAST TO ORGANIZE/SHIFT ACROSS THE MID MO VALLEY AND CENTRAL PLAINS REGION MAINLY DURING THE SECOND HALF OF THE PERIOD...AS MN/IA VICINITY CYCLOGENESIS OCCURS IN RESPONSE TO THE UPPER TROUGH EJECTION. WITH THIS STORM SYSTEM MOVING INTO/ACROSS THE PLAINS WHERE A MOIST/UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR WILL RESIDE...EXPECT DEVELOPMENT OF STRONG/SEVERE STORMS TO BECOME WIDESPREAD THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AND EVENING HOURS.

sections.title: ERN WY/SD/SWRN MN/WRN IA SWD TO THE TX/OK PANHANDLES
sections.text: AFOREMENTIONED/EARLY EJECTION OF INITIAL/MINOR TROUGHING INTO THE NEB VICINITY MAY SUPPORT EARLY/ONGOING STORMS...THUS SOMEWHAT COMPLICATING THE CONVECTIVE FORECAST IN THIS AREA. HOWEVER...WITH EARLY CONVECTION LIKELY TO NOT DISRUPT THE AIRMASS ENTIRELY...LIKELIHOOD FOR AT LEAST LIMITED DAMAGING WIND/HAIL RISK SHOULD EXTEND ACROSS THIS AREA THROUGH MUCH OF THE DAY AND INTO THE EVENING. FARTHER S -- INTO KS AND POSSIBLY THE TX/OK PANHANDLE VICINITY...A MOIST AND ESSENTIALLY UNDISTURBED BOUNDARY LAYER WILL SUPPORT AFTERNOON MIXED-LAYER CAPE VALUES IN THE 1500 TO 2500 J/KG RANGE. GIVEN THE INCREASING ASCENT FOCUSED ACROSS THE HIGH PLAINS...EXPECT STORMS TO DEVELOP BY MID AFTERNOON AND THEN SPREAD EWD ACROSS THE KS VICINITY WITH TIME. WITH LOW-LEVEL SLY FLOW TOPPED BY MID-LEVEL WLYS INCREASING TO AT OR ABOVE 40 KTS...DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WILL BE SUFFICIENT FOR ORGANIZED/SUPERCELL STORMS. THOUGH TORNADO RISK SHOULD REMAIN LIMITED TO SOME DEGREE BY RELATIVELY MODEST LOW-LEVEL SHEAR...ROTATING STORMS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS CAN BE EXPECTED -- PARTICULARLY DURING THE EARLY PORTIONS OF THE CONVECTIVE EVENT. outlooks.summary: SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO AFFECT LOCATIONS FROM THE MIDDLE MISSOURI VALLEY INTO THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT. VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING STRAIGHT-LINE WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY HAZARDS...THOUGH A COUPLE OF TORNADOES ARE ALSO POSSIBLE.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: THE MOST SALIENT UPPER-AIR FEATURE TO SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT IS A SHORT-WAVE TROUGH WHICH WILL TRANSLATE FROM THE NRN INTER-MOUNTAIN REGION AND GREAT BASIN INTO THE UPPER MS AND MID/LOWER MO VALLEYS DURING THE DAY ONE PERIOD. MORNING WATER VAPOR IMAGERY AND MODEL GUIDANCE INDICATE THAT THIS TROUGH IS COMPRISED OF SEVERAL SMALLER-SCALE VORTICITY MAXIMA WHICH WILL EMERGE FROM THE ROCKIES AT DIFFERENT TIMES...LEADING TO A COMPLEX CONVECTIVE EVOLUTION ACROSS THE ADJACENT CNTRL PLAINS. AT THE SURFACE...A LEE CYCLONE INITIALLY OVER NERN CO WILL UNDERGO A SLIGHT DEEPENING WHILE DEVELOPING NEWD ALONG A QUASI-STATIONARY FRONT INTO W-CNTRL MN BY SUNRISE MONDAY. THIS LOW PRESSURE WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY A COLD FRONT WHICH WILL ADVANCE EWD ACROSS THE DAKOTAS AND SWD THROUGH THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS. A SECONDARY SURFACE LOW WILL DEEPEN OVER WRN KS TODAY AHEAD OF THE COLD FRONT...ALONG A DRYLINE WHICH WILL STRETCH FROM WRN KS TO WRN TX.

sections.title: MID-MO VALLEY TO SRN PLAINS TODAY INTO TONIGHT
sections.text: A COMPLEX FORECAST SCENARIO IS UNFOLDING THIS MORNING OWING TO THE EARLY EMERGENCE OF A LEAD VORTICITY MAXIMUM INTO THE CNTRL HIGH PLAINS. DCVA ASSOCIATED WITH THIS FEATURE IN CONJUNCTION WITH WAA AND MOISTURE FLUX AT THE TERMINUS OF A 50 KT SLY LLJ ARE LIKELY CONTRIBUTING TO AN INCREASE IN TSTM DEVELOPMENT OVER WRN NEB AS OF 12Z. AND LATEST MODEL GUIDANCE SUGGESTS THAT THESE FORCING MECHANISMS WILL SUPPORT AN INCREASE IN STORM COVERAGE AND INTENSITY TODAY INVOF THE STATIONARY FRONT DRAPED ACROSS SRN SD/NRN NEB. GIVEN THE STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND MUCAPE OF AROUND 1500 J/KG OBSERVED ON THE 12Z NORTH PLATTE SOUNDING...THE POTENTIAL WILL EXIST FOR ORGANIZATION OF STORMS INTO AN MCS WITH AN ASSOCIATED THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS SPREADING EWD INTO THE MO RIVER VALLEY LATER THIS AFTERNOON INTO EVENING. TO THE S OF THE ABOVE-MENTIONED CONVECTIVE REGIME...THE COMBINATION OF BOUNDARY-LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 50S TO LOWER 60S...STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...AND DAYTIME HEATING ARE EXPECTED TO YIELD A MODERATELY UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR BY AFTERNOON WITH MLCAPE VALUES APPROACHING 1500-2500 J/KG. outlooks.summary: SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO AFFECT LOCATIONS FROM THE MIDDLE MISSOURI VALLEY INTO THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN GREAT PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT. VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING STRAIGHT-LINE WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY HAZARDS...THOUGH A COUPLE OF TORNADOES ARE ALSO POSSIBLE.

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE MIDDLE MO VALLEY
sections.text: A COMPLEX PATTERN HAS DEVELOPED SURFACE AND ALOFT ACROSS THE ROCKIES INTO THE PLAINS...AS A STRONG UPPER TROUGH NOW OVER THE NRN/CENTRAL ROCKIES MOVES EWD ACROSS THE NRN AND CENTRAL PLAINS THROUGH TONIGHT. ACTIVE CONVECTION HAS CONTINUED THROUGH THE MORNING FROM THE CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE UPPER MS VALLEY WITH A MORE PERSISTENT CLUSTER OF STRONG STORMS OVER PARTS OF WRN/CENTRAL NEB WHERE LOW LEVEL WARM ADVECTION AND CONVERGENCE AT THE NOSE OF A SLY LOW LEVEL JET HAS AIDED SYSTEM MAINTENANCE. THE OVERNIGHT AND MORNING STORMS HAVE CREATED MULTIPLE LOW LEVEL BOUNDARIES FROM SRN MN/NWRN IA SWWD INTO SWRN NEB/NERN CO WHICH WILL LIKELY PROVIDE FOCUS REGIONS FOR CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT AND INTENSIFICATION THIS AFTERNOON. 12Z AREA SOUNDINGS EXHIBIT STEEP LAPSE RATES FROM THE ROCKIES EWD INTO THE PLAINS OVERLAYING A MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER WITH SURFACE DEW POINTS NEAR 60 OVER WRN KS/ERN CO AND INTO THE MID/UPPER 60S OVER ERN PARTS OF NEB AND KS. VISIBLE IMAGERY SHOWS LIMITED CLOUDS OVER MUCH OF IA AND ERN NEB WHERE STRONG DIABATIC HEATING IS OCCURRING DOWNSTREAM FROM THE CENTRAL NEB CONVECTIVE SYSTEM...WITH ADDITIONAL STRONGER HEATING EXPECTED FROM WRN/SOUTH CENTRAL KS INTO ERN CO WHERE GENERAL

sections.title: SRN PLAINS
sections.text: A FEW STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO AFFECT PARTS OF MAINLY NRN OK LATE THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING AS ACTIVITY SPREAD/DEVELOPS SEWD FROM KS. THERE IS MORE UNCERTAINTY REGARDING STORM DEVELOPMENT OVER THE ERN TX PANHANDLE WHERE A STRONGER CAP IS IN PLACE. SEVERAL CONVECTION-ALLOWING MODELS INDICATE ISOLATED STORMS DEVELOPING LATE THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING IN THIS AREA WITH ACTIVITY POSSIBLY MOVING SEWD INTO WRN OK BEFORE WEAKENING. GIVEN STRONG INSTABILITY/VERTICAL SHEAR ANY SUSTAINED UPDRAFT WILL LIKELY ATTAIN SUPERCELL CHARACTERISTICS WITH A THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND STRONG WINDS. ..WEISS/DEAN.. 06/01/2014

outlooks.summary: SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO AFFECT LOCATIONS FROM THE MIDDLE MISSOURI VALLEY INTO THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN GREAT PLAINS THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT. VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING STRAIGHT-LINE WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY HAZARDS...THOUGH A COUPLE OF TORNADOES ARE ALSO POSSIBLE.

sections.title: ERN CO...WRN KS...SWRN NEB
sections.text: AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY CONTINUES TO DRIFT SWD FROM NRN KS INTO NERN KS AS A CLUSTER OF STORMS CONTINUES EWD ACROSS SRN NEB. STRONG HEATING PERSISTS FROM CO INTO WRN KS...WITH ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS NOW OVER E CNTRL CO...AND AN EXPANDING CU FIELD INTO WRN KS. OTHER INCIPIENT STORMS WERE INITIATING ALONG THE DRYLINE OVER EXTREME SERN CO...AND THESE WILL LIKELY BECOME SEVERE AS WELL AS THEY SHIFT INTO KS. VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS APPEAR LIKELY WITH ALL THIS ACTIVITY. THE GREATEST THREAT OF AN ISOLATED TORNADO WOULD APPEAR TO BE IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY BUT UNDERCUTTING OUTFLOW AND MARGINAL T/TD SPREADS SHOULD KEEP ANY THREAT BRIEF. FOR MORE INFORMATION SEE MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 774 AND 776.

sections.title: NERN NEB INTO NRN IA AND SRN MN AND WI
sections.text: EXPANDED LOW TORNADO PROBABILITIES EWD ALONG THE BOUNDARY WHERE BRIEF TORNADOES WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE. ALSO EXTENDED LOW SEVERE HAIL AND WIND PROBABILITIES EWD INTO WI WHERE NUMEROUS STORMS WERE DEVELOPING WITH A FEW HAIL CORES NOTED ON RADAR. FOR MORE INFORMATION SEE MESOSCALE DISCUSSION 775.

sections.title: OK/TX PANHANDLES INTO NWRN OK
sections.text: THUNDERSTORMS CONTINUE TO FORM UPSTREAM INTO ERN CO WITH MORE VIGOROUS ACTIVITY EXPECTED LATER TODAY INTO WRN KS. A ROBUST SLY LOW-LEVEL JET...COUPLED WITH STRONG DESTABILIZATION AND NW-SE ORIENTED DEEP-LAYER SHEAR VECTORS SUGGESTS STORMS WILL TURN/PROPAGATE SEWD INTO OK LATER THIS EVENING AND OVERNIGHT. NOCTURNAL CAPPING WILL BE A LIMITING FACTOR AS TO HOW FAR S STORMS CAN GET...BUT THE AREA N OF I-40 AND WEST OF I-35 APPEARS TO HAVE THE GREATEST THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL. ..JEWELL.. 06/01/2014 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1131 AM CDT SUN JUN 01 2014/

sections.title: DISCUSSION
sections.text: TWO BANDS OF STRONG/LOCALLY SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING ACROSS THE CENTRAL U.S. ATTM...ONE SHIFTING SEWD ACROSS NWRN NEB AND ADJACENT NERN CO AND A SECOND WHICH IS ADVANCING EWD ACROSS KS AS A NE-SW LINE. RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL PERSISTS LOCALLY WITH THE NEB/NERN CO BAND OF STORMS...THOUGH EXPECT THESE STORMS TO GRADUALLY DIMINISH LATER THIS EVENING. FARTHER SE...RISK FOR DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL WILL LIKELY PERSIST THROUGH MOST OF THE EVENING...AS A FAVORABLY UNSTABLE AIRMASS AHEAD OF THE CONVECTION AND AN INCREASE IN THE SLY LOW-LEVEL JET OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS SUPPORTS STORM PERSISTENCE. ..GOSS.. 06/02/2014

mesoscale_discussions.summary: PERSISTENT EARLY DAY TSTM CLUSTER OVER CNTRL NEB APPEARS TO BE IN THE PROCESS OF INTENSIFYING WITH ADDITIONAL SURFACE-BASED STORMS FORMING IN CONFLUENCE BANDS TO THE S/E. STEEP LAPSE RATES IN THE WARM SECTOR AND STRENGTHENING DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WILL SUPPORT SEVERE HAIL TRANSITIONING TO SEVERE WINDS WITHIN LINE SEGMENTS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LARGELY UNORGANIZED MCS OVER CNTRL NEB TO S-CNTRL SD HAS APPEARED TO INTENSIFY OVER THE PAST HALF-HOUR WITH STORM INITIATION OCCURRING ALONG DIFFERENTIAL HEATING CORRIDORS TO THE S INTO N-CNTRL KS AND E INTO CNTRL NEB. GIVEN STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES WHERE OVERTURNING HAS NOT YET OCCURRED...ISOLATED SEVERE HAIL WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE IN THE EARLY LIFE-CYCLE OF UPDRAFTS. DEEP-LAYER WINDS HAVE INCREASED IN TIME-SERIES OF KUEX VWP DATA. CONTINUED DEVELOPMENT OF STORMS WILL LIKELY YIELD A STRENGTHENING COLD POOL AND WITH SURFACE TEMPERATURES NEAR 90 DEG F IN THE DOWNSTREAM WARM SECTOR...THE RISK FOR SEVERE WIND GUSTS SHOULD INCREASE LATER THIS AFTERNOON.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STRONG THUNDERSTORMS WILL CONTINUE THIS AFTERNOON...WITH A THREAT OF AN ISOLATED/BRIEF TORNADO AND MARGINALLY SEVERE WIND/HAIL. THE LIMITED MAGNITUDE OF THE THREAT MAKES WW ISSUANCE UNCERTAIN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING AT 1830Z ALONG AND NORTH OF AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY RUNNING FROM NWRN IA ENEWD INTO WRN WI. MODERATE INSTABILITY HAS DEVELOPED NEAR AND SOUTH OF THE BOUNDARY...WITH 1000-1500 MLCAPE NOTED PER RECENT OBJECTIVE MESOANALYSIS. RELATIVELY WEAK DEEP-LAYER SHEAR SHOULD CONTINUE TO RESULT IN GENERALLY DISORGANIZED STORM STRUCTURES...THOUGH STORMS INTERACTING WITH THE BOUNDARY WILL RESULT IN THE CONTINUED RISK OF AN ISOLATED/BRIEF TORNADO...IN AN AREA OF FAVORABLE OVERLAP BETWEEN STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND ENHANCED SURFACE VORTICITY. TORNADOES HAVE BEEN OBSERVED IN THIS VICINITY DURING THE LAST HOUR OVER WINNEBAGO/KOSSUTH COUNTIES IN NRN IA. THE POTENTIAL FOR UPSCALE GROWTH IS UNCLEAR IN THIS REGIME...THOUGH ANY SUCH EVOLUTION WOULD RESULT IN A SOMEWHAT ENHANCED RISK FOR DAMAGING WIND. MARGINAL LAPSE RATES SHOULD LIMIT THE SEVERE HAIL RISK. WW ISSUANCE IS UNCERTAIN AT THIS TIME GIVEN THE DISORGANIZED NATURE OF THE STORMS AND EXPECTED BRIEF NATURE OF THE TORNADO THREAT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED TO SCATTERED SUPERCELLS WILL LIKELY DEVELOP BY 21Z WITH VERY LARGE HAIL AND PERHAPS A TORNADO. UPSCALE GROWTH INTO AN MCS WITH POTENTIAL BOWING SEGMENTS REMAINS EXPECTED...YIELDING AN INCREASING RISK FOR SEVERE WINDS THIS EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TSTM INITIATION HAS COMMENCED AROUND 30 SE LIC ALONG A SURFACE TROUGH WHICH HAS GENERALLY BEEN WELL-MODELED BY CONVECTION-ALLOWING GUIDANCE. ADDITIONAL STORMS WILL FORM ACROSS WRN KS IN N/S-ORIENTED CONFLUENCE BANDS AS SURFACE TEMPERATURES WARM THROUGH THE 80S AND LOWER 90S AMIDST UPPER 50S TO LOWER 60S DEW POINTS...AND PERHAPS ALONG A SWD-SAGGING OUTFLOW BOUNDARY NEAR THE KS/NEB BORDER. WITHIN A QUITE STEEP LAPSE RATE ENVIRONMENT...MODERATELY STRONG BUOYANCY IS EVIDENT WITH MLCAPE OF 2000-3000 J/KG. TIME-SERIES OF VWP DATA FROM KGLD HAS SHOWN A TENDENCY FOR VEER-BACK PROFILES IN THE WAKE OF THE LEAD MCS OVER CNTRL NEB. HOWEVER...WITH A BELT OF STRENGTHENING MID-LEVEL WLYS EMANATING ACROSS THE SRN ROCKIES...WIND PROFILES ARE ALREADY CONDUCIVE TO SUPERCELLS FARTHER S PER 18Z DDC RAOB. RELATIVELY LARGE SURFACE TEMPERATURE/DEW POINT SPREADS WILL TEND TO FAVOR OUTFLOW-DOMINATED UPDRAFTS. OVERALL SETUP SHOULD YIELD VERY LARGE HAIL AS THE PRIMARY INITIAL RISK...TRANSITIONING TO SEVERE WINDS WITH POTENTIAL FOR A BOWING MCS THIS EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SEVERE WIND/HAIL RISK MAY EXTEND N OF WW 201 ACROSS PORTIONS OF SERN SD/SWRN MN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: 19Z SURFACE ANALYSIS INDICATES ROBUST PRESSURE RISES AT KONL/KODX BEHIND A SSW/NNE-ORIENTED CONVECTIVE LINE FROM PIERCE COUNTY NEB TO TURNER COUNTY SD. A POCKET OF GREATER SURFACE HEATING IS EVIDENT TO THE N OF THIS LINE...AWAY FROM THE CLOUD SHIELD ASSOCIATED WITH THE WSW/ENE-ORIENTED CONVECTIVE LINE FROM NWRN IA TO SERN MN. ALTHOUGH 0-3 KM WINDS ARE WEAK IN FSD VWP DATA...THE ORIENTATION OF THE LINE WITH RESPECT TO STRONGER MID-LEVEL SWLYS MIGHT SUPPORT A SEMI-ORGANIZED SEGMENT EVOLVING NEWD ACROSS THE BUFFALO RIDGE. ..GRAMS.. 06/01/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE WIND/HAIL RISKS WILL PERSIST MAINLY WITHIN ERN/SRN PORTIONS OF WW 201. NWRN PORTION IS LIKELY SUFFICIENTLY STABILIZED WITH A NEGLIGIBLE RISK.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: COMPLEX/MESSY CONVECTIVE STRUCTURES SHOULD PERSIST AMIDST A LARGE-SCALE MCS ACROSS THE UPPER MIDWEST TO CNTRL PLAINS. A THREAT FOR ISOLATED SEVERE WIND/HAIL SHOULD EXIST ACROSS PORTION OF ERN NEB INTO WRN IA WHERE OVERTURNING HAS YET TO OCCUR AMIDST SURFACE TEMPERATURES IN THE MIDDLE TO UPPER 80S AND DEW POINTS IN THE MIDDLE 60S. HOWEVER...WEAKER DEEP-LAYER SHEAR WITH ERN EXTENT /0-6 KM OF AROUND 20 KT IN OAX VWP DATA/ WILL TEMPER THE OVERALL AMPLITUDE OF THE SEVERE RISK COMPARED TO FARTHER SW. REGENERATIVE CLUSTERS WILL ALSO CONTINUE ACROSS THE SRN PORTION OF WW 201 GIVEN INTENSE WAA ATOP THE CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW WITH LOWER 90S SURFACE TEMPERATURES IN THE WARM SECTOR AND 60S WITHIN THE COLD POOL. HERE...LARGE HAIL WILL BE THE PRIMARY RISK WITH THE MORE ROBUST UPDRAFTS...BUT SEVERE WIND RISK COULD INCREASE WHERE FORWARD PROPAGATION IS FAVORED NEAR THE KS/NEB BORDER. ..GRAMS.. 06/01/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ONGOING TSTMS ACROSS NE IA MAY STRENGTHEN WITH A RESULTANT INCREASE IN THE DAMAGING WIND THREAT ACROSS CNTRL IA AS THE STORMS MOVE EWD/SEWD. SCENARIO IS FAIRLY UNCERTAIN BUT TRENDS ACROSS THE REGION WILL BE MONITORED CLOSELY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LINE OF TSTMS MOVING THROUGH NE IA HAS SHOWN SOME SIGNS OF ACCELERATING FORWARD AS IT ENCOUNTERS AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM PREVIOUS CONVECTION. RECENT FORWARD SURGE IN CHEROKEE AND O'BRIEN COUNTIES WAS GENERALLY NEWD...PLACING THE STORM BEHIND THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. HOWEVER...ACTIVITY WOODBURY AND MONONA COUNTIES HAS ALSO SURGED FORWARD WITH MORE INTERACTION WITH THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY LIKELY. FAVORABLE INTERACTION WITH THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WILL RESULT IN INCREASED UPDRAFT STRENGTH AND STORM ORGANIZATION WITH A RESULTANT INCREASE IN THE DAMAGING WIND AND SVR HAIL THREAT AS THE STORM CONTINUES EWD. THERE IS CONSIDERABLE UNCERTAINTY WITH THIS SCENARIO...OWING PRIMARILY TO WEAK BULK SHEAR AND STORM ORGANIZATION CURRENTLY OBSERVED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: STRONG/LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS AND MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE AS THUNDERSTORMS TRACK SOUTH/SOUTHEAST ACROSS THE SRN NEB PANHANDLE INTO SW NEB/FAR NE CO THE NEXT 1-3 HOURS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG DEEP LAYER SHEAR AND A MODERATELY UNSTABLE DOWNSTREAM AIRMASS HAS ALLOWED THUNDERSTORMS MOVING OFF HIGHER TERRAIN TO ORGANIZE INTO A FORWARD PROPAGATING LINE ACROSS THE SRN NEB PANHANDLE. DOWNSTREAM OF THESE STORMS TEMPERATURES IN THE MID 70S TO LOW 80S WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE MID TO UPPER 50S ARE PRESENT...AND DCAPE VALUES QUICKLY INCREASE TO OVER 1000 J/KG. A SHORTWAVE IMPULSE EJECTING ACROSS SRN/CNTRL WY IS ALSO EVIDENT IN WATER VAPOR IMAGERY. STRONG TO LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS ARE POSSIBLE FOR AT LEAST 1-3 HOURS AS THE LINE CONTINUES TO SURGE S/SEWD. AS CONVECTION MOVES FURTHER AWAY FROM STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH THE SHORTWAVE IMPULSE...AND AS DIURNAL COOLING COMMENCES STORMS SHOULD BECOME INCREASINGLY ELEVATED AND THE DAMAGING WIND THREAT WILL DIMINISH. ADDITIONALLY...AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY EARLIER MOVED SOUTHWARD ACROSS SW NEB INTO NE CO. THE 20Z RAOB FROM LBF SHOWS THAT THE BOUNDARY LAYER BELOW ABOUT 800 MB HAS BECOME MORE STABILIZED. THIS WILL FURTHER FAVOR STORMS BECOMING INCREASINGLY ELEVATED WITH TIME. STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES ALSO MAY SUPPORT SOME INSTANCES OF MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL WITH STRONGER UPDRAFTS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: RADAR AND OBSERVATIONAL TRENDS SUGGEST THE DEVELOPMENT OF A STRONG CONVECTIVE LINE IS ONGOING WITH A PRIMARY SVR THREAT OF DAMAGING WINDS. HAIL AND EMBEDDED TORNADOES COULD ALSO OCCUR.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT RADAR IMAGERY SUGGESTS UPSCALE GROWTH IS UNDERWAY WITH THE DEVELOPMENT OF A BOW FROM CNTRL KS NEWD INTO SE NEB. ACTIVITY ON THE NRN EDGE OF THE LINE HAS SHOWN A STRONG EWD PUSH WITH EMBEDDED MESOVORTICIES ACROSS REPUBLIC COUNTY KS. THIS EWD PUSH MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH THE DEVELOPMENT OF A REAR-INFLOW JET WITH A BOOKEND VORTEX NOTED FARTHER N ACROSS THAYER AND JEFFERSON COUNTIES. UEX VAD CORROBORATES THIS SCENARIO WITH 40 TO 50 KT EWD FLOW AT 2-3 KFT RECENTLY SAMPLED. AIRMASS AHEAD OF THE DEVELOPING CONVECTIVE LINE IS CHARACTERIZED BY MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES IN EXCESS OF 7 DEG C PER KM AND DEWPOINTS IN THE MID 60S. BULK SHEAR IS ORIENTED FAVORABLY FOR FORWARD-PROPAGATION WITH AN INCREASING LOW-LEVEL JET EXPECTED TO AID INFLOW AS WELL. ADDITIONALLY...STORMS ACROSS SW KS HAVE SHOWN A TREND TOWARDS UPSCALE GROWTH. SYNTHESIS OF THESE TRENDS AND OBSERVATIONS RESULTS IN THE MOST LIKELY SCENARIO OF CONTINUED UPSCALE GROWTH AND FORWARD-PROPAGATION OF A STRONG CONVECTIVE LINE EXTENDING FROM SW KS NEWD INTO FAR SE NEB. SOME EMBEDDED MESOVORTICIES ARE POSSIBLE BUT THE PRIMARY SVR THREAT APPEARS TO BE DAMAGING WINDS. LARGE HAIL WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE. ..MOSIER.. 06/01/2014 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A LINE OF STORMS ARCING SOUTHWESTWARD FROM SE NEB INTO CENTRAL KS WILL CONTINUE TRACK EWD THE NEXT FEW HOURS INTO ERN KS...EVENTUALLY MOVING INTO THE KANSAS CITY METRO AREA BY 03Z. STRONG/DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THESE STORMS. A DOWNSTREAM WW AND/OR AERIAL EXTENSION MAY BE NEEDED IF TRENDS CONTINUE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A LINE OF THUNDERSTORMS ARCING FROM SE NEB SWWD ACROSS CENTRAL INTO SW KS WILL CONTINUE TRACKING E/SE THIS EVENING. THIS BAND OF CONVECTION HAS SHOWN SIGNS OVER THE LAST HOUR OF BECOMING BETTER ORGANIZED OVER N-CNTRL KS WITH EVIDENCE OF A DEVELOPING REAR INFLOW JET PER UEX VWP. THIS ALIGNS WELL WITH HI-RES MODEL GUIDANCE...WHICH DEVELOPS SEVERAL BOWING FEATURES TRACKING EWD ACROSS NE KS INTO NW MO THIS EVENING AS A SHORTWAVE TROUGH SHIFTS E/NE ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS.
